---
title: Live examples
description: Write an example once; the page shows its code and runs it, in the page or in an isolated iframe, optionally editable.
---

import { Live } from '../../../../components/live';

`<Live>` turns one piece of code into two things: a code block (Expressive Code, with title and copy button)
and the running result. **The code shown is the code that runs**: the component reads the source back out of the
rendered code block, so there is no second copy to drift. Every example on this page is a `<Live>`.

The demo modules used below live in `example/apps/live-assets/` and are served at `/apps/live-assets/` by the
static-apps mirror. Point your own examples at your library the same way (for example `/pixel/src/runtime/pixel-sprite.js`).

## Write an example

Import the component, then put a fenced code block inside it. Leave a blank line after the opening tag and before
the closing one, so MDX treats the block as Markdown. MDX never touches the inside of a fence, so `<script>`,
`{braces}` and template literals are safe.

````mdx title="my-page.mdx"
import { Live } from '../../components/live';

<Live caption="A custom element, defined by a module">

```html title="hello.html"
<script type="module" src="/apps/live-assets/hello-badge.js"></script>
<hello-badge name="docs"></hello-badge>
```

</Live>
````

<Live caption="A custom element, defined by a module">

```html title="hello.html"
<script type="module" src="/apps/live-assets/hello-badge.js"></script>
<hello-badge name="docs"></hello-badge>
```

</Live>

The import path is relative to your page. The fence's language and meta work as usual (`title="…"`, line markers).

### Modules run once per page

Inline examples share the page, so the browser's module map applies: a module loaded by several examples
(`<script type="module" src>`, the `modules` prop, or a runner) is evaluated once, and its `customElements.define`
never runs twice. External classic scripts (`<script src>` without `type="module"`) are de-duplicated the same
way. The badge counts how often its module was evaluated:

<Live caption="Same module, second example">

```html
<script type="module" src="/apps/live-assets/hello-badge.js"></script>
<hello-badge name="again" tone="green"></hello-badge>
```

</Live>

## Inline mode: part of the page

`mode="inline"` (the default) renders straight into the page. Scripts run (classic and module, inline and
external), and the example can reach anything else on the page: here a custom element hops along the cards
inside the example **and** along <strong data-hop>this word</strong> and the
<strong data-hop>next heading</strong> outside it. This is what a library like Pixel Studio's `<pixel-stage>`,
where characters walk on page elements, needs.

<Live caption="Reaching outside the example" height={140}>

```html
<script type="module" src="/apps/live-assets/hop-dot.js"></script>
<div style="display: flex; gap: 1rem; align-items: flex-end; padding-top: 2rem">
  <div data-hop style="flex: 1; height: 60px; border: 2px solid; border-radius: 8px"></div>
  <div data-hop style="flex: 1; height: 90px; border: 2px solid; border-radius: 8px"></div>
  <div data-hop style="flex: 1; height: 40px; border: 2px solid; border-radius: 8px"></div>
</div>
<hop-dot targets="[data-hop]"></hop-dot>
```

</Live>

The preview opts out of Starlight's Markdown styles (it carries `not-content`), but it is still the page: a
`<style>` in an inline example applies to the whole page, and ids must be unique on it. When an example needs
its own document, use an iframe.

## Iframe mode: isolated

`mode="iframe"` renders into a sandboxed iframe that sizes itself to its content. The iframe gets Starlight's
colour and font tokens (`--sl-color-*`, `--sl-font`) and follows the theme switch, so it still looks like the
page. Use `head` for styles, import maps or scripts, `modules` for module URLs, and `base` so relative paths
resolve against your assets.

<Live
  mode="iframe"
  caption="Isolated styles, a base URL, and auto-height"
  base="/apps/live-assets/"
  head="<style>button { font: inherit; padding: .3rem .8rem } li { color: var(--sl-color-accent-high) }</style>"
>

```html
<script type="module" src="hello-badge.js"></script>
<hello-badge name="iframe"></hello-badge>
<p><button id="more">Add a line</button> — the frame grows with its content.</p>
<ul id="list"></ul>
<script>
  let n = 0;
  document.getElementById('more').onclick = () => {
    const li = document.createElement('li');
    li.textContent = `line ${++n}`;
    document.getElementById('list').append(li);
  };
</script>
```

</Live>

Errors inside the iframe (thrown exceptions, rejected promises, a script or stylesheet that fails to load) are
shown under the preview.

The default sandbox is `allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-forms allow-modals`. Same-origin is
what lets the frame load modules and fetch assets from your site without CORS headers; it also means the frame
could reach the page, so it isolates styles and globals, not trust. For code you do not trust, pass
`sandbox="allow-scripts"` and serve the assets it needs with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

## Editable examples

`editable` turns the code into a text area. Edits re-run the example after a pause (`debounce`, 300 ms by
default), the copy button copies what you typed, and **Reset** brings back the original. Tab inserts two spaces;
press Escape and then Tab to move on. Editable HTML examples are best in an iframe, which starts from a clean
document on every run.

<Live mode="iframe" editable caption="Edit me" base="/apps/live-assets/">

```html
<script type="module" src="hello-badge.js"></script>
<hello-badge name="you" tone="orange"></hello-badge>
<p>Change the name, or try <code>tone="green"</code>.</p>
```

</Live>

## Custom runners

With `runner="/url/to/module.js"`, the source is not HTML: it is handed to the module's `run` function, which
renders it. That is how a library shows a spec, a config or a small DSL being interpreted live. The code is
typically JSON (the default `lang` when a runner is set).

```js title="runner.js"
/**
 * @param {string} source       the code, as shown or as edited
 * @param {HTMLElement} mount   an empty element to render into
 * @param {import('…/components/live/types').LiveContext} ctx
 */
export function run(source, mount, ctx) {
  const spec = JSON.parse(source); // throw to show an error under the preview
  // …render into mount…
  ctx.status('ok: 3 frames', 'ok'); // optional one-line status
  return () => {}; // optional cleanup, called before the next run
}
```

`ctx` carries:

| Field | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | The example's id. |
| `mode` | `inline` or `iframe`. |
| `options` | The `options` prop, as given. |
| `reducedMotion` | `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The example re-runs when it changes. |
| `theme` | `light` or `dark`. The example re-runs when the page theme changes. |
| `base` | The `base` prop as an absolute URL, else the page URL. |
| `signal` | An `AbortSignal`, aborted when this run is replaced or the example is removed. |
| `status(message, level)` | Shows a line under the preview; `level` is `ok`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. |

Errors thrown by `run` (or by the promise it returns) are shown under the preview; the page carries on. The
module is loaded once per page (or once per iframe in iframe mode).

The playground below uses a tiny pixel-art engine. It is editable, side by side on wide screens, and starts only
when scrolled into view (`lazy`). With reduced motion it shows the first frame instead of animating.

<Live
  runner="/apps/live-assets/pixel-engine.js"
  editable
  lazy
  preview="side"
  options={{ scale: 12 }}
  caption="A runner: JSON in, pixels out"
  id="pixel-playground"
>

```json title="blink.json"
{
  "palette": { "k": "#23212c", "y": "#f6c945", "w": "#ffffff" },
  "fps": 3,
  "frames": [
    [".yyyy.", "yyyyyy", "ywkywk", "yyyyyy", "yykkyy", ".yyyy."],
    [".yyyy.", "yyyyyy", "ykkykk", "yyyyyy", "yykkyy", ".yyyy."],
    [".yyyy.", "yyyyyy", "ywkywk", "yyyyyy", "yyyyyy", ".yyyy."]
  ]
}
```

</Live>

An error looks like this (this spec uses a colour that is not in its palette; fix it by adding `"r"` to the
palette):

<Live runner="/apps/live-assets/pixel-engine.js" editable mode="iframe" options={{ scale: 10 }} caption="A runner error, shown inline">

```json
{
  "palette": { "k": "#23212c" },
  "frames": [["k.k", ".r.", "k.k"]]
}
```

</Live>

## Layout

- `preview="above"` (default), `"below"` or `"side"`. Side by side needs about 36rem of width and falls back to
  stacked on narrow screens.
- `caption` adds a caption with a `#` link. `id` sets the anchor; without it the id comes from the caption or
  title (`#live-…`), so links stay stable while the text does.
- `height` sets the preview's minimum height (a number is pixels), which avoids layout shift for examples that
  load assets, and is the iframe's height before it measures itself.
- `lazy` waits until the example is near the viewport. Use it for heavy examples.

<Live preview="below" caption="Preview below the code">

```html
<p style="margin: 0">The preview can sit under the code, too.</p>
```

</Live>

## In .astro pages (and code from files)

`.astro` files have no Markdown fences; pass the source as `code` instead (`lang` and `title` go with it). This
also works in MDX, for example with a file imported raw:

```astro title="src/pages/index.astro"
---
import { Live } from '../components/live';
import demo from '../demos/hello.html?raw';
---
<Live code={demo} title="hello.html" caption="Straight from a file" />
```

<Live
  code={`<script type="module" src="/apps/live-assets/hello-badge.js"></script>\n<hello-badge name="code prop" tone="purple"></hello-badge>`}
  title="from-a-prop.html"
  caption="Source passed as the code prop"
/>

## All props

| Prop | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | the fenced child | The source. |
| `lang` | `html` (`json` with a runner) | Highlighting language for `code`. |
| `title` | | Code frame title for `code` (for fences use `title="…"` in the fence). |
| `caption` | | Caption with an anchor link. |
| `id` | from caption/title/source | Stable id and anchor. |
| `mode` | `inline` | `inline` or `iframe`. |
| `preview` | `above` | `above`, `below` or `side`. |
| `editable` | `false` | Editable code that re-runs, with Reset. |
| `runner` | | Module URL exporting `run(source, mount, ctx)`. |
| `options` | `{}` | Passed to the runner as `ctx.options`. |
| `modules` | `[]` | Module URLs to load first. |
| `head` | | Extra HTML for the iframe's `<head>`. |
| `base` | page URL | Base URL for relative paths in the iframe; `ctx.base` for runners. |
| `sandbox` | see above | iframe sandbox tokens. |
| `height` | | Minimum preview height. |
| `lazy` | `false` | Start when scrolled into view. |
| `debounce` | `300` | Milliseconds between the last keystroke and the re-run. |

Styling uses Starlight's tokens (`--sl-color-*`, with fallbacks on pages outside Starlight), so a theme that
sets them restyles the examples too. All component styles are scoped under `live-example`.
